record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.context_brief: Quadratic bound for k-blocked point sets
record.original_question: Does every k-blocked point set have O(k^2) points?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4 Every k-blocked point set has O(k^2 ) points.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane. Given a finite set $P$ of points, say that a point $x \in P$ blocks two other points $v, w \in P$ if $x$ lies in the interior of the line segment $vw$. For an integer $k \ge 1$, call $P$ a $k$-blocked set if there exists a coloring $c : P \to \{1,2,\dots,k\}$ using exactly $k$ colors such that, for every pair of distinct points $v, w \in P$, one has $c(v) = c(w)$ if and only if some point of $P \setminus \{v,w\}$ blocks $v$ and $w$ (equivalently, lies on the open segment $vw$).

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that for every integer $k \ge 1$, every $k$-blocked set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ satisfies $|P| \le C k^2$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that every k-blocked point set has O(k^2) points was posed by Aloupis, Ballinger, Collette, Langerman, Pór, and Wood (2010/2013). They verified small cases: every 2-blocked set has at most 3 points, every 3-blocked set at most 6, and every 4-blocked set at most 12 (tight). No proof or counterexample of the general quadratic bound appears in the literature; the conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Blocking Coloured Point Sets
status_evidence.snippet: A point set P is k-blocked if each point of P is assigned one of k colours, such that distinct v,w in P have the same colour iff some other point in P blocks v and w. We prove every 4-blocked set has at most 12 points (tight).
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the definition and small-k results, conjecturing a quadratic bound in general.

status_evidence.title: Blocking Colored Point Sets (Springer chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture that every k-blocked set has bounded size as a function of k; proves the bound for k <= 4.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the conjecture is stated and only verified for small k.
